He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] who previously played non-professionally for the Cold Hearts in [[Overtime Elite]] during what would have been his senior year in high school. Dillingham became a guard for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] during the 2023-2024 season.{{Cite web |last=Tucker |first=Kyle |title=So Kentucky might really be back, huh? |url=https://theathletic.com/5142705/2023/12/17/kentucky-win-unc-calipari-dillingham/ |access-date=2024-04-24 |website=The Athletic |language=en}} ==Early life and high school career== Dillingham was born and raised in [[Hickory, North Carolina]].Byerly, Justin. (November 30, 2021). [https://hoopseen.com/news/player/202111/dillingham-set-commit-possible-wolfpack-lock Dillingham Set to Commit, Possible Wolfpack Lock]. ''HoopSeen''. Retrieved January 17, 2022. His father Donald is [[African Americans|African American]] and mother Lia is originally from [[Samoa]].{{cite web |last1=Cyphers |first1=Luke|title=Kanye West Donda Debacle Divides a Kentucky Hoops Signee’s Family |url=https://www.sportico.com/leagues/basketball/2022/kanye-west-donda-academy-basketball-robert-dillingham-father-1234698512/ |website=Sportico: The Business of Sports |access-date=May 30, 2024 |date=December 16, 2022}} Rob played basketball for Combine Academy in [[Lincolnton, North Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Robert Dillingham's Star is on the Rise |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/robert-dillingham-combine-academy-point-guard-2023-allen-iverson |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=August 25, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Siner |first1=Jeff |title=Combine Academy's Robert Dillingham is more than a scorer |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article247115477.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=December 21, 2020}} Dillingham emerged as one of the top players in his class by his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=O'Brien |first1=Patrick |title=2023 Robert Dillingham is already becoming one of the hottest prospects in his class with college programs |url=https://phenomhoopreport.com/2023-robert-dillingham-is-already-becoming-one-of-the-hottest-prospects-in-his-class-with-college-programs/ |website=Phenom Hoop Report |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=August 26, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 21.2 points, 4.9 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 2.1 steals per game, leading his team to a 29–3 record and a non-association state title. He was named ''[[The Charlotte Observer|Charlotte Observer]]'' Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Wertz Jr. |first1=Langston |title=All-Observer boys basketball: Combine's Robert Dillingham is player of the year |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article251329648.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=May 12, 2021}} For his junior year, he transferred to [[Donda Academy]], [[Kanye West]]'s school in [[Simi Valley, California]]. For his senior year, he transferred to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_Elite Overtime Elite]in [[Atlanta, Georgia]] which was powered by [https://www.subjectvirtual.com Subject Virtual School]. ===Recruiting=== Dillingham was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Fowler |first1=Chapel |title=Can an unofficial visit keep UNC basketball in the lead for five-star point guard Robert Dillingham? |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/06/29/2023-five-star-point-guard-robert-dillingham-unofficially-visiting-unc-basketball-hubert-davis/7787135002/ |website=[[The Fayetteville Observer]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=June 29, 2021}} On December 1, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] over offers from [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. He became the second highest-ranked recruit in program history, behind [[Dennis Smith Jr.]] On March 19, 2022, Dillingham announced his decommitment from NC State and reopened his recruitment.{{cite web|title=Five-star guard Robert Dillingham decommits from NC State|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Robert-Dillingham-decommitment-NC-State-analysis-184758356/|first=Brandon|last=Jenkins|date=March 19, 2022|access-date=March 28, 2022}} On June 24, 2022, Dillingham committed to Kentucky over the offers of [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. He became Kentucky's second commit in the 2023 recruiting class.{{cite [[Kanye West]], and signed with [[Overtime Elite]], a professional basketball league for late high school and early college-level players.{{Cite web |title=Kentucky Recruit Robert Dillingham Leaving Donda Academy for Overtime Elite |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10054524-kentucky-recruit-robert-dillingham-leaving-donda-academy-for-overtime-elite |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}} He joined the Overtime Cold Hearts, one of the six teams in the league.{{Cite web |title=After becoming the first Overtime Elite player to sign with Kentucky, Rob Dillingham makes OTE debut |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/11/12/after-becoming-the-first-overtime-elite-player-to-sign-with-kentucky-rob-dillingham-makes-ote-debut/ |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=Zags Blog}} Dillingham made his OTE debut for the Cold Hearts on November 11, recording six points, three rebounds and three steals in a 92–84 loss to the YNG Dreamerz.{{Cite web |title=YNG Dreamerz Stay Perfect with Win Over Cold Hearts |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/e1dd9e44-03b1-44a2-aca3-2a83d2e26e75 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=Overtime Elite}} After spending one season with the [[University of Kentucky]], Dillingham would declare his entry into the [[2024 NBA draft]]. ==National team career== Dillingham led the United States to a gold medal at the [[2021 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Mexico. He was named [[most valuable player]] after averaging 15.7 points, 6.2 assists and 3.2 steals per game.{{cite web |title=USA's Dillingham wins U16 MVP, headlines All-Star Five |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/u16americas/2021/news/usa-dillingham-wins-u16-mvp-headlines-all-star-five |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=August 30, 2021}} He posted a team-record 31 points, six rebounds, four assists and three steals in a 90–75 win against [[Argentina men's national under-17 basketball team|Argentina]] in the final.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=High school basketball: Robert Dillingham's 31-point outburst leads USA U16 National Team to seventh consecutive gold |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/D0S7-HId8EaLcMPVO21wJw/high-school-basketball--robert-dillinghams-31-point-outburst-leads-usa-u16-national-team-to-seventh-consecutive-gold.htm |website=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=August 29, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] | 32 || 1 || 23.3 || .475 || .444 || .796 || 2.9 || 3.9 || 1.0 || .1 || 15.2 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ukathletics.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/dillinham-rob/ Kentucky Wildcats bio] *[https://www.usab.com/players/robert-dillingham USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Dillingham, Rob}} [[Category:2005 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from North Carolina]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Overtime Elite players]] [[Category:People from Hickory, North Carolina]] [[Category:Point guards]]
